title: The Tiny Armchair
logline: Ted's fourteen-month scale model of the apartment, tiny hand-painted gang included, is found crushed the morning after game night, and nobody will confess. Detective Mosby interrogates his four suspects, each of whose versions of 1:14 a.m. makes the teller a saint, and the only detail they all agree on is the one Ted refuses to believe: he sleepwalks.
coldOpen: Kids, in the spring of 2013, somebody in our apartment destroyed fourteen months of my work. There were four suspects, four alibis, and four completely different versions of the same night.

couch.line: Let me guess. Everybody remembers it differently.
Everybody remembers it wrong. I'm the only reliable witness, Penny. I was asleep.

guests.name: Anneke
guests.role: Barney's Dutch dream date, a structural engineer and swimwear model who exists, at least that night, only in Barney's version of events; breathes architectural compliments, every one of them about Barney

scenes.summary: Sunday morning after game night. Ted comes out to find his 1:12 scale model of the apartment crushed: landing collapsed, tiny armchair flattened. It's not a dollhouse. Ted lays out the evidence: a buffalo sauce thumbprint on the tiny fridge (Marshall), a red hair in the tiny bathroom (Lily), a scotch ring on the roof (Robin), and nothing at all from Barney, the professional. Ted declares himself the only reliable witness: he slept like a baby. The gang exchange a look.

beats.line: For fourteen months, I'd been building a perfect scale model of our apartment. On Sunday morning, it was less perfect.
Good morning, little apartment! Two more days until your gallery debut!
No. No, no, no, no, no!
Ted. Quieter. My hangover is filing a noise complaint.
The landing's collapsed. The tiny armchair is crushed. The tiny piano is in the tiny kitchen.
Oh no. Not the tiny piano.
Ted, it's a dollhouse. Get some glue.
It is not a dollhouse. It is a one-to-twelve scale architectural model.
With dolls in it.
They're scale figures, Robin. Tiny me has a cable-knit sweater. Ted did the cables with a needle.
It's the creepiest thing I've ever loved.
Ted, you texted me crime scene at seven a.m. on a Sunday. I suited up for a body.
Oh. Somebody broke your dollhouse.
It's not a dollhouse!
Relax, little buddy. It's balsa wood. Nobody died.
Fourteen months, Barney. One of you did this. So. Who would like to confess?
Can I go first?
Yes! Thank you, Marshall.
I didn't do it.
Then explain Exhibit A. A buffalo sauce thumbprint on the tiny refrigerator.
Lots of people have thumbs, Ted.
Exhibit B. A long red hair in the tiny bathroom.
Lots of things have red hair. Ginger cats. Elmo. Mars.
Mars doesn't have hair.
Not with that attitude.
Exhibit C. A scotch ring on the roof.
Everybody drinks scotch.
Robin, nobody drinks scotch. You drink scotch. You're holding one right now.
This is a different scotch.
And you, Barney. No prints. No hair. No rings. Not a trace.
Because I'm a professional.
Ted, how do you know you didn't do it?
Because I went to bed at midnight and slept like a baby. I'm the only reliable witness.
What was that look?
Nothing.

scenes.summary: Ted interrogates Marshall and Lily in the booth while Robin and Barney heckle from the bar. The downstairs neighbor heard a crunch at 1:14 and a man saying 'oh no, little buddy'. Marshall's version: he's a saint who ate salad, and a sleepwalking Ted calls him the best roommate in history. Ted insists he doesn't sleepwalk. Marshall cracks: he opened the tiny fridge looking for tiny food. Lily's version contradicts: Marshall ate thirty-one wings over the model, and sleepwalking Ted puts Lily in charge of everything. Lily cracks: she gave tiny Lily two inches and cheekbones, and fixed tiny Robin's hair. Accurately. Barney drags Robin off to a cab, Ted chases them, and Marshall and Lily agree never to tell Ted he sleepwalks: he tucks in the toaster.

beats.line: That night, I set up an interrogation room at MacLaren's. Same booth. But I'd moved the ketchup.
Marshall Eriksen. Where were you at one fourteen a.m.?
Why one fourteen?
Because Mr. Pakula downstairs heard a crunch through his ceiling. Then a man's voice said, oh no, little buddy.
Okay. It was one fourteen. I remember because I was checking the time. Responsibly.
Everyone, please. Let's give Ted's beautiful model some room. Out of respect.
Marshall, you're so responsible. And you've only had salad all night.
Marshall, you've changed me. Tomorrow I'm calling my mom and planting a tree.
And you were right about Bigfoot.
Marshall. You're the best roommate in the history of roommates.
And now I'll turn in. Early. Like a man with nothing on his thumbs.
I said you were right about Bigfoot?
You did. It was beautiful. There wasn't a dry eye in the house.
Also, that never happened. I don't sleepwalk.
Totally. Weird detail. No idea where that came from.
Marshall. The thumbprint. On the tiny refrigerator.
Okay! I opened the tiny fridge!
I wanted tiny food, Ted! Fourteen months and your fridge is empty! Who lives like that?
It's a model, Marshall. The fridge doesn't open.
It does now.
That's not how it happened, Ted. I was the only sober one.
Hey Lily, watch me eat thirty-one wings directly over Ted's model.
Marshmallow, no. That's art.
Lily, how is your hair so much better than mine?
Lily. You should be in charge. Of everything.
I know, Ted. Go back to bed.
Lily! Six of those wings were celery!
Lily. That red hair was stuck to tiny Lily. Who now has cheekbones.
Okay, fine! I touched her up! You made her so short!
It's to scale.
Your scale is rude.
And while I was in there, I fixed tiny Robin's hair.
Fixed it how?
Accurately.
Robin. Barney. You're next.
Love to, Ted. Can't. Robin and I are sharing a cab.
We are now.
Nobody leaves an active investigation!
Should we tell him he sleepwalks?
And ruin the best part of our week?
Tuesday he tucked the toaster into bed and told it it was a very good toaster.
And he's right, Marshall. It is a very good toaster.

scenes.summary: Ted squeezes into Robin and Barney's cab and orders the driver to circle the park until someone confesses. Robin's version: she's the sober guardian while Barney does shots off the tiny piano, sleepwalking Ted calls her the coolest, and she sets her glass down on the coffee table. Which had a model on it. The green roof is now a green coaster. Barney's version: everyone else passed out, he gives a tour to Anneke, a Dutch structural engineer and swimwear model, and sleepwalking Ted calls him legendary. Anneke was in Rotterdam. Ted notices every version has him in the doorway at 1:14; Robin and Barney tell him he sleepwalks. He storms out to prepare his big reveal. Robin and Barney: he's going to do the drawing-room thing.

beats.line: Ted, you can't just jump into somebody's cab.
I can, I did, and I hurt my knee. Driver, circle the park until somebody confesses.
Robin. One fourteen a.m. Where were you?
On the couch. Sober. Alert. Guarding your dollhouse.
Model.
Woo! Shots off the tiny piano!
Marshall, let's move into the dollhouse!
We'll be so tiny and so rich!
Guys. Respect the architecture.
Robin. You're the only one I trust. And the coolest. By a lot.
I know, Ted. Go to bed.
I'll just set my drink down on the coffee table.
The model was on the coffee table. Where on the coffee table, Robin?
The part with a roof on it.
It's flat, Ted. It was asking for it.
It's a green roof! It had hand-planted tiny sedum!
Now it's a green coaster.
A glass didn't crush the landing. Barney. Your turn.
Fine. But I warn you. My version is legen—
Just tell it.
Barney, I have never seen a man so gentle with a load-bearing wall.
Anneke, I am a load-bearing wall.
Barney. You're legendary. And Robin was wrong about you.
I know, little buddy. Back to bed.
Ignore the snoring, Anneke. Lightweights. I was the only sober one.
Shall we? This place is far too small for a man of my scale.
Who is Anneke?
A Dutch structural engineer and swimwear model. She was there in spirit.
And in body?
Rotterdam.
Can we just stay in Uncle Barney's version?
No.
Wait. Every version has one thing in common.
Everyone's drunk except the person telling it?
Me. One fourteen. In my bedroom doorway, saying something nice about whoever's talking.
Because you were in the doorway, Ted. You sleepwalk.
I do not sleepwalk!
Ted, last month you woke up on the roof holding a waffle iron.
I was stargazing.
In your red cowboy boots. And only your red cowboy boots.
Driver, pull over. Tomorrow night, my apartment, nine o'clock. I will name the culprit.
He's going to do the drawing-room thing.
He's been waiting his whole life to do the drawing-room thing.

scenes.summary: Ted gathers the suspects and finds them all guilty of something: the tiny fridge, the tiny plastic surgery, the green coaster. But none of it crushed the landing. Then the clue nobody noticed: tiny Barney is missing. Who says 'little buddy'? Barney confesses, and the truth plays out: he cancelled on the real Anneke to sit alone with the model, found tiny Barney in his own tiny armchair, and sleepwalking Ted told him he always has a chair here. Overwhelmed, Barney sat down. On the third floor. He hid it because his apartment has one chair, on purpose, and nobody had ever built him one. Ted: it's a model of us. Barney returns tiny Barney in a tuxedo; he has eleven. Ted concedes it's a dollhouse. Future Ted: the only person who told the truth was asleep. Penny: last night he told the toaster it always has a chair here. It does.

beats.line: I suppose you're wondering why I've gathered you all here.
You texted us. It said, I suppose you're wondering why I've gathered you all here.
Four suspects. Four stories. And every one of you is guilty of something.
beats.title: The Collapse of the Landing: A Forensic Review

beats.line: Burglarized is a strong word. It was empty, Ted. It's still empty.
But none of that collapsed the landing. That took something heavy. About a hundred and eighty pounds.
Two-twenty, thank you. It's mostly heart.
And one clue none of you noticed. Fourteen months, I know every piece. There were four tiny figures in that model.
There are now three.
Tiny Barney.
Maybe he left. He's a very popular little guy. He probably had a date.
He was glued into his armchair, Barney.
And which one of us calls everybody little buddy?
Barney.
Fine. It was me. But it's not what you think.
Anneke. I can't do our call tonight. Something came up. No, it's a guy. He's about three inches tall.
Mm. Nice coaster.
Look at you. Tiny suit. Tiny scotch. Your own little chair.
He made you a chair, buddy.
That's your chair, Barney. You always have a chair here.
Ted? Are you awake?
Is it raining?
Okay. I just need to sit down for a second. Right here.
Oh no. Little buddy.
You sat on it?
I sat on the third floor, Ted. Emotionally and physically.
Wait. I said that? In my sleep?
Then you went into the kitchen and tucked in the toaster.
Barney, why didn't you just tell me?
Because then I'd have to explain why I was whispering to a doll of myself at one in the morning.
Ted, I've built my whole life so nobody needs me around after breakfast.
Nobody ever built me a chair before.
Barney. It's not a model of the apartment. It's a model of us. Of course you have a chair.
Okay, stop. This shirt is nine hundred dollars and it does not absorb.
Here. He's been staying with me. He's been through a lot.
Barney. He's wearing a tuxedo.
It's a gallery opening, Ted. Show some respect.
You had a tailor make a tiny tuxedo?
Marshall. He has eleven.
Tonight I rebuild the landing. And tiny Barney goes back in his chair.
In his dollhouse.
In his dollhouse.
Kids, five people were in that apartment that night, and four of them lied. The only one telling the truth was fast asleep.
Dad, last night you sleepwalked into the kitchen and told the toaster it always has a chair here.
And it does.
